issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs students to call setup_env() with no parameters (problem_statement.md line 22). The reference solution, however, calls setup_env with one pushed argument (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 12-15: 'push 1' then 'call setup_env') and also declares 'extern setup_env'. This is a parameter/signature mismatch: students following the written instruction (no-arg call) will produce different code than the solution, and the solution's one-argument call contradicts the specification. This discrepancy can confuse students about the intended call convention and may lead to incorrect reference behavior or stack-management issues during execution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the expected setup_env signature consistent across artifacts. Recommended: update the solution to call setup_env() with no parameters (remove 'push 1' before the call) so it matches the problem statement, and keep or add 'extern setup_env' where appropriate. Alternatively, if setup_env genuinely requires an argument, update the problem statement to document that it takes one parameter (and show its meaning) and update the template to declare 'extern setup_env' or instruct students to add the extern declaration.
